title: Kenney Jones - Wikipedia
notes: Kenneth Thomas Jones, born 16 September 1948, Whitechapel, London. A founder of the Small Faces (1965-1969), then the Faces until their end in 1975; the Who's drummer from November 1978, after Keith Moon's death, on Face Dances and It's Hard and the tours of 1979-1982, Live Aid (1985) and the 1988 BPI award; replaced by Simon Phillips for the 1989 tour. Daltrey: 'I just felt he wasn't the right drummer for the Who'; his playing 'usually straighter and less frenetic than Moon's'. The Law with Paul Rodgers (1991), the Jones Gang (2001-). He 'virtually taught' Zak Starkey and gave him one of Moon's kits. Rock and Roll Hall of Fame 2012 with the Small Faces/Faces. Memoir: Let the Good Times Roll (2018).

title: Small Faces - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in East London in 1965 by Steve Marriott, Ronnie Lane, Kenney Jones and Jimmy Winston (Ian McLagan replacing Winston in 1966); 'one of the most acclaimed and influential mod groups of the mid-1960s'; Whatcha Gonna Do About It (1965), All or Nothing (1966, number one), Itchycoo Park and Tin Soldier (1967), Lazy Sunday (1968) from Ogdens' Nut Gone Flake, a UK number one. Jones: drums, percussion (1965-1969, 1975-1978).

title: Faces (band) - Wikipedia
notes: Formed in 1969 when Lane, Jones and McLagan took on Rod Stewart and Ronnie Wood from the Jeff Beck Group; four studio albums to their break-up in 1975 (A Nod Is As Good As a Wink... to a Blind Horse, 1971, with Stay With Me; Ooh La La, 1973). Jones: drums, percussion (1969-1975 and the reunions to the 2020s); Stay With Me with Stewart and Wood at the 2020 Brit Awards.

title: Kenney Jones: British Drumming Royalty (Adam Budofsky, Modern Drummer, 18 August 2011)
notes: His recordings in his own words. Stay With Me: 'It's 16ths on the hi-hat all the way through, and in order to get the groove right you have to get the tempo bang-on.' 'The Faces are unique in playing so laid back'; 'Tempos could be a nightmare in the Faces'. 'You Better You Bet in particular was a good recording.' 'Changing the backbeat between the snare and the tom was just my handle on it.' I Know I'm Losing You: 'lots of press rolls and triplets with the bass drum'. Influences: 'Al Jackson will remain my hero till the day I'm gone'; 'Before anything else, I was very much influenced by jazz'; 'Booker T. & the MG's was always on my record player'. Technique: 'For rock gigs I play with my left stick turned around the other way [butt end]'; 'I also hit the drums a lot harder than most players'; 'my tuning is completely different from most drummers''. The 1966 sessions: 'just a couple of overheads and a snare mic'.

title: Kenney Jones - Drums (kenneyjones.com)
notes: His own list of kits: a white Premier Olympic first; a silver glitter Ludwig in the early Small Faces (their first TV, Thank Your Lucky Stars); a black Ludwig that had been Brian Bennett's; Rogers in the Small Faces; an 18-inch blonde Ludwig 'jazz kit'; with the Faces a tartan Premier, white Premier and white Yamaha kits and three blonde Ludwigs; a white Premier with the Who in 1979, then a black Yamaha for most of his Who years, with a gong. Small Faces and early Faces sizes: bass drum 14x22, tom 9x13, floor tom 14x14, snare 5.5x14. Sabian cymbals ('fuller and brighter').
